summary: Sandy grey-brown bedding mortar, gritty and matte, as in the joints between bricks, stones and tiles.
_comment: A cement-lime bedding mortar: grey-brown binder paste holding sharp sand (grains 0.3 to 1.5 mm, mostly tan quartz, a few dark and a few white) with small air voids, matte and gritty. One article for brick, stone and tile joints. Opaque: a rough porous solid. The maps are generated (L2, gen_mortar_cement.py; the wish list said L3, but the scans that name mortar are brick walls, which are assemblies); nothing in the 0.1 m tile is larger than a few mm, so its repeat shows no grid. The mean albedo (0.33, 0.30, 0.25) is a judgement, set darker than concrete because a joint sits in shadow; it is tinted down for a dark or sooted joint. A pale lime mortar for older rooms is lighter than this base and a tint cannot go above 1, so it would be its own article. Carries cracks (overlay 1, damage) gated by the Crevice mask, at 0 (C1). It carries NO dust layer on purpose: the asset tooling's ask is that a joint never lightens, and a dusty joint reads near-white. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Mortar_Cement_Clean_Base_s01_v01

sources.why: Mean linear albedo (0.33, 0.30, 0.25), about sRGB 155, 148, 136, for a grey-brown sandy cement-lime mortar, darker than Physically Based Concrete (0.51) because a joint sits in shadow; mean roughness 0.93 for a matte gritty face; specular_ior 1.5 as for Physically Based Concrete. Physically Based has no mortar entry. meters_per_tile 0.1 is the s01 option's length; the generator makes the tile at that size.
